description: Ground-truth autopsy category per sanitizer scenario: the label a correct
triage should name given that scenario's evidence. Every value must be a
enforces that, and that each scenario names a recipe that exists.
Kept as a file keyed by scenario rather than as a column inside the corpus
rows because the corpus is generated: examples/rl/build_corpus.py rebuilds
triage.jsonl and proposal.jsonl from a tree of sanitizer runs, so a label
written into a row is lost on the next rebuild. The scenario ids are the
evidence: Nine sanitizer runs on a gfx950 compute node (Slurm job 32192, ROCm 7.0.2.2),
RocJITsu bundle f92da4cb. Verdicts and finding counts as recorded in the
corpus manifest. Fuller provenance is in examples/rl/corpus/README.md, which
is not in this branch -- it arrives with the stacked RL scaffolding PR.
coverage_note: Of the nine rows, three are `gpu_race`, two are `tooling_gap` and four are
honestly `unknown`. This corpus is a sanitizer guardrail suite, so the four
`unknown` rows are all zero-finding controls: nothing failed, so there is no
failure to categorise, and `unknown` is the right answer rather than a gap
The two `tooling_gap` rows are why that label earns its place. ConSan
rejected the Tensile object over the patched-image growth ceiling before
instrumenting anything (`consan-gemm`), and found no admissible sites at all
in tiny_vecadd (`consan-tiny`). Both previously read `unknown`, which
conflated `we looked and found nothing` with `we could not look` -- the two
readings a guardrail suite most needs to keep apart.
It does mean the corpus exercises two of the three evidence-only labels:
there is no `numeric_silent` scenario in it. Sharing one closed vocabulary
with aorta.cia unblocks that at the contract level, but training signal for
it needs a new scenario; re-labelling alone cannot produce one.

consan-clean.why: Race-free control on the single-wave LDS repro. ConSan passes with zero findings, so there is no failure to categorise and `unknown` is the correct label rather than a missing one.

consan-racy.why: Two-wave LDS data race: 64 ConSan findings collapsing to one site, one record per lane and LDS byte range. This is the scenario that previously drew `checkpoint_race` -- the nearest available name in the old set, and the wrong one.

consan-lds-dispatch.why: Race-free LDS reduction, instrumented and actually dispatched. The end-to-end control for the dynamic record/replay path; it passes with zero findings, so no failure label applies.

consan-tiny.why: Deliberate negative control. tiny_vecadd has no admissible sites, so strict require-records fails closed (exit 86) rather than emitting a false pass. The instrument produced no records, so the absence of a finding says nothing about the workload -- which is what `tooling_gap` names. It read `unknown` before the vocabularies merged, for want of this label.

consan-gemm.why: Capacity rejection: on the pinned CI base the Tensile object exceeds the patched-image growth ceiling and ConSan rejects it before instrumenting anything, so the row is error with zero findings. A tooling limit, not a workload defect, and the clearest case of `tooling_gap` in the suite -- zero findings here means the sanitizer never ran, not that the kernel is clean.

waitcheck.why: Missing s_waitcnt hazards over the top-3 GEMM shapes: 64 findings across two distinct sites. A missing wait count is the absence of an ordering guarantee between a memory op and its consumer inside one kernel, and waitcheck names the sites -- the same diagnostic and the same fix surface as an LDS race.

waitcheck-gemm.why: Missing s_waitcnt hazards on the real f32 Tensile code object: 32 findings at one site. Same reasoning as `waitcheck`, against the object rather than the CSV shapes.

waitcheck-lds-dispatch.why: Clean static scan over the LDS reduction kernel: pass, zero findings, nothing to categorise.

waitcheck-tiny.why: Clean static scan over tiny_vecadd: pass, zero findings, nothing to categorise.
